data.body:
Implemented with `paradoxal-unquenched-snowmonkey` (ad8d-4274-ef43-4f44) as one change, since both
land in `infra/terraform/user_data.sh`. Rebased onto `origin/main` after change 2649 (bug d614,
`e6b4ff07da5d`) hardened `resolve_ebs_device` in the same file; that work is intact and its tests
still pass.

**How the asymmetry was closed.** The assertion did not get COPIED to the `/var/gerrit` call site —
it moved INTO `mount_ebs_volume`, as a new `require_mounted`. That is deliberate: the defect was
that a guard living at one call site is absent from the other by default, so a third volume added
later would have inherited the same hole. Now every caller gets it and a call site cannot opt out.
The standalone `mountpoint -q` block after the gate-scratch call is gone as redundant;
`test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py`'s `"mountpoint -q" in script` assertion still holds, because the
string moved rather than disappeared.

- **AC1** — `require_mounted` runs after `mount -a` for both volumes and returns non-zero.
- **AC3** — the two failures are now distinguishable by BOTH message and exit code: a genuine
  `mount -a` error is "mount -a reported an ERROR while mounting <mp>" and returns 3; a silent
  `nofail` skip is "<mp> is NOT a mount point after a CLEAN mount -a -- its nofail fstab entry was
  skipped silently" and returns 4. Previously every failure printed "could not resolve NVMe device",
  which was actively misleading for a mount that resolved fine and then did not take.
- **AC2** — the oracle in `tests/unit/test_user_data_device_resolution_d614.py` (reused, not
  duplicated) now models all three `mount -a` outcomes rather than always succeeding, `MOUNT_SKIPS=1`
  being the real nofail-skip mode. Deleting the `ASSERT-MOUNT-TOOK` line makes the skipped mount
  report SUCCESS again, which is the reported defect. Against `origin/main`'s script, 9 of the new
  tests are RED.
- **AC4** — `infra/scripts/check-mounts.sh`, invokable as `sudo infra/scripts/check-mounts.sh`.
  Portable by construction: plain shell plus util-linux with a `/proc/mounts` fallback, no AWS API
  calls (so it works with no credentials, mid-incident, on a host whose IMDS is unhappy) and no CI
  provider. It distinguishes "the directory does not exist" from the DANGEROUS state — the
  directory exists, so every consumer looks healthy, on root. `provision-restore.md` step 4b now
  covers both volumes and points at it, and says plainly not to treat "Gerrit responds" as evidence.

Why the separate script is not redundant with the in-script assertion: `user_data.sh` runs at FIRST
BOOT only. Every later boot re-runs `mount -a` from `/etc/fstab` with no witness at all, which is
exactly the pending stop/start case this ticket flagged.

**Live-host note, unchanged by this ticket and NOT acted on:** `nvme2n1` (`vol06780b8557d1416b7`) is
attached raw — no filesystem, unmounted — and `/etc/fstab` has no gate-scratch line, so gate scratch
has been running on root. That is `renowned-corked-hapuku` (`dcc3-75ee-26ce-4840`) and is the
operator's call. No action was taken on the running host.
